title: Which Payment an Insured Plan of Care Refund Is Returned Against
content:
For a refund of credit on an Insured Plan of Care, the payment the refund is returned against, and so its ceiling, is chosen in this order:

| Condition on the plan's payments | Payment returned against | Ceiling on the refund |
|---|---|---|
| The most recent card payment on the plan was made no more than the payer program's card refund window ago | That card payment | Its amount |
| No card payment is that recent, and the plan carries a check payment | The most recent check payment | Its amount |
| Otherwise | The most recent payment on the plan | Its amount |

The refundable credit is never larger than the payment it is returned against.

**Card refund window by payer program.** 120 calendar days on every payer program — Commercial PPO, Commercial High-Deductible, Commercial POS, Commercial HMO, Medicare Part B, Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Managed Care Plans of Care. A card payment made 120 days ago is within the window; one made 121 days ago is not.

## Hypothetical illustrations (today 2026-06-15)

1. Card payment of $60.00 on 2026-05-01 and a later ACH payment of $200.00 on 2026-06-01: the card payment is within 120 days, so the refund is returned against it and is at most $60.00.
2. Card payment of $60.00 on 2026-01-10 (156 days ago), check payment of $90.00 on 2026-02-01 and cash payment of $25.00 on 2026-05-20: the card is outside the window and the plan carries a check payment, so the refund is returned against the $90.00 check.
3. Card payment on 2026-01-10 and a cash payment of $25.00 on 2026-05-20, no check: the refund is returned against the most recent payment, the $25.00 cash payment.
